title: Built this 2D Metroidvania prototype to showcase and hopefully find and build a core team with people with different skillsets who are interested in making games who aren't anti AI.
author: BeingComfortablyDumb
selftext:
Hello!

I am a solo developer and I started my own studio "Mythic Motion". I have been a game designer before AI. A lot of unfinished games that never saw the light of day during those times but started to make polished deployable games on App/Play stores. I currently have 4 games live on both stores and deployed 2 games made here for Reddit.

I wanted to try building a game bigger in scope and I had this idea lurking around in my mind and decided to give it a try. Using my own skills alongside AI tools to build a prototype I could share with others and hopefully find people who want to work on this alongside me! I used Codex and ComfyUI workflows to build the assets, Claude to implement and merge everything. I was a game designer before so making GDD and Design Bible was always a must for me before any project. Once that is setup, my role mostly was then testing, debugging, adding/removing levels and stuff, making the map and the progression!

This is not a promotion since it's only a demo prototype. It's still not what I have imagined and pretty unpolished still I'd say. I am currently looking for someone well versed with 2D assets and animations, a sound engineer and a writer to help expand and fill the story.

You can play the demo here on Itch: [https://mythicmotion.itch.io/crimson-ruin](https://mythicmotion.itch.io/crimson-ruin)

Please do let me know what you think and what I should add remove. There is a lot of work still to be done so be please keep that in mind while judging!

Also, I am not looking to hire for these roles. The core team should be partnership/equity-based and any hiring/freelancing that needs to be done will be decided upon together.

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
so my method for doing like draining I think if you want some advice,  put in like a mortal combat finisher stun.  right they start wobbling on the spot at 0hp  and you have a couple of seconds to 'use' them,  the character reaches out and  i mean if it was me.. rips the living blood from thier veins with magic.  to do that you tell your ai, make a few curvy spline paths and spam a bunch of blood/gore sprites down them, have them scale down as they approach the character.  you have them center on the mouth maybe.   
needs maybe... 2 character poses, 3 alts to show a little secondary action for the suck/ drinking action.  and you just play like 2 poses (picture the twitching bodies on spikes in doom, 2 frames twitch, does alot of work)  


and there you go. blood suck mechanic  for when the player feels like being brutal.  :)

happy to chat whenever. had a look at your game too.  
overall goood impression. i think... some quality variance,  cracks on the area pasage at the start feel like standin graphics compared to the rest.

action, movements and fighting feels close but a little disjointed. you can solve that I think by making teh character a little floatier.  this gives them a little air time  and if you double jump you get some more to make decisions on what to hit.

other things you can do.  wall jumps, mantling.  these can help alot making it feel more actiony and less   stand in this exact spot to make it.... if that makes sense.

Ive done a platformer and I found that  airtime helped make you feel more powerful, attack chaining  and boosts in mid air add to that.   then you are getting into devil may cry enemy juggling but tell me thats not fun   


anyway man, looking good, hit me up in a dm or whatever if ya want.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Played it. Here's some thoughts, with the caveat that I love these games but am completely horrible at them: 

 \- The parrying is super difficult. If you want that to be the case, that's fine, but for me it was next to impossible to parry anything. So, for me personally, I wouldn't want to play this very much because the parry also feels essential (to get a sense of my speed with something like this, my favourite game with a parry mechanic is Absolum. It's not a Metroidvania at all, but at moments it does feel like one). 

 \- The art direction is great; the art itself is a very mixed bag. The UI is incredibly well-done; the walking and jumping animations are nice and fluid; the basic attack combat animation, unfortunately, feels anemic and the parry doesn't have enough visual impact. Enemy designs feel a bit uninspired, but I like that the attacks and movement are all extremely readable. The environments also look great. 

 \- The platforming is impressively good. I'm played dozens of 'metroidvania' games from this sub; your is the first one that has passed a basic feels good benchmark for the platforming, which is arguably the most important thing to get right in the genre. Good job.

 \- ...I am too awful at the game to get past the first boss, so I can't comment on whatever mapping system and/or branching traversal system you've implemented. Choice of game difficulty is something I feel like I have no business critiquing because I enjoy easier games, and it would be ridiculous to expect nobody wants to make a hard game - at the same time, good criticism has to come from an honest assessment based on my own experience, not the hypothetical experience of someone who might enjoy a harder game... 

 \- ...I didn't have a good time. The presentation is lovely, easily several cuts above the stuff that gets posted here, and it may be fully the case that this game isn't for me, but I wouldn't play this again in its current state. Partly that's because the combat doesn't feel satisfying, but if I'm being honest, this game is too hard for me to enjoy even if the combat felt immaculate. 

  
Nice work. I wish you success on the project.

replies.author: BeingComfortablyDumb
replies.body:
Thank you for the kind words and suggestions. I'll definitely make changes in the next update. 

The parry is intentionally made harder, maybe I can add attack animations or a visual que or something. 

The art is not close to what I had in mind but had to work with the AI tools I had. This is the best I can sum up currently. I'll probably tried paid tools to see if that makes it any better. I'd hope to find person for this actually but well, gotta work with what I've got. 

I spend quite a bit if time on the level designs so really appreciate your words on the platforming. Tho the assets designs could be much better imo. 

The hard difficulty is inspired by Silksong, Blasphemous. I'd rather add difficulty levels but I can make the gameplay a bit smoother and responsive so it feels easier.
